federal_note: Federal programs (DTC, Child Disability Benefit, RDSP, Canada Child Benefit, Canada Disability Benefit for adults, Jordan's Principle, Inuit Child First) apply everywhere; see data/programs.json.

programs.name: Supplement for Handicapped Children (SEH)
programs.what: Monthly tax-free money for families of a child with a disability. Everyone gets the same amount. Your income does not matter.
programs.amount: 2026: $241/month ($2,892/year) per child; retroactive up to 11 months (Retraite Québec, checked 2026-10-17).
who: The disability makes daily life much harder and will last at least a year.
steps: Apply to Retraite Québec online or by form, with a report from your child's health worker.
links: Retraite Québec: SEH amount and payment
programs.nickname: SEH (Quebec monthly money for kids with disabilities)

programs.name: Supplement for Handicapped Children Requiring Exceptional Care (SEHNSE)
programs.what: Extra money on top of SEH for kids with very high care needs.
programs.amount: 2026 yearly: Tier 1 $14,580, Tier 2 $9,696 (Retraite Québec key data table, checked 2026-10-17).
who: Your child already gets SEH and needs a very high level of care.
steps: Apply to Retraite Québec with the special form.
programs.nickname: SEHNSE (Quebec extra money for kids needing a lot of care)

programs.name: Family Allowance (Allocation famille)
programs.what: Tax-free money for families with kids. You need it to get SEH.
programs.amount: No fixed amount published; check the official page.
who: You live in Quebec, have kids under 18, and file a Quebec tax return.
steps: It usually starts when you register a birth. If not, apply to Retraite Québec.

programs.name: Social Solidarity Program / Basic Income Program
programs.gov: Quebec (Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale)
programs.what: Monthly money for adults whose health makes it very hard to work.
programs.amount: No fixed amount published; check the official page.
who: Adults with serious health limits, confirmed by a doctor's report.

programs.name: Jordan's Principle (First Nations children)
programs.what: Money from the federal government for First Nations kids. It can pay for therapy, respite (a break for you while someone else cares for your child), talking devices, and equipment. It works in every province, on or off reserve.
programs.amount: Case by case; no fixed amount.
who: Your child is First Nations and under 19
steps: Call 1-855-572-4453. The line is open 24 hours a day.
Or apply online on the Indigenous Services Canada website.
programs.nickname: Jordan's Principle (help for First Nations kids)
